data.name: Lavish
data.gender_notes: Lavish is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Lavish is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Lavana' which means 'to cover, to adorn'. This name is bestowed upon a child who is expected to bring wealth, prosperity, and luxury in their life. In Hindu mythology, Lord Vishnu is often described as being lavish in his blessings and protection. The name Lavish carries the meaning “Abundance, Wealth, Luxury” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Mythological tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lavish usually hope their child will grow to embody abundance, wealth, luxury and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: May your life be abundant with blessings and luxuries.
data.etymology: Lavish belongs to the Mythological linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Abundance, Wealth, Luxury.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lavish total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

Often, names in Hindu culture have deep meanings that represent the hope and aspirations for a child's future. "Lavish" encapsulates the desire for a life full of material prosperity and spiritual enrichment.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Lavish signifies the abundance and generosity of the Universe. It is a reminder of the divine blessings and provisions that are available to us. The Hindu god, Lord Vishnu, is often invoked for his lavish and opulent nature. He is the preserver of the Universe and the embodiment of wealth and abundance. The name Lavish serves as a spiritual reminder to be grateful for the blessings in our lives, and to strive for a balance between material and spiritual prosperity.

In this story, Lavish is a rich merchant who gives away all his wealth to help a poor man in need, and is later rewarded with great riches. This story illustrates the Buddhist virtues of generosity and selflessness.
